arxiv-2201-05613.title: The Dark Side of the Language: Pre-trained Transformers in the DarkNet
arxiv-2201-05613.creator: Leonardo Ranaldi, Aria Nourbakhsh, Arianna Patrizi, Elena Sofia Ruzzetti, Dario Onorati, Michele Mastromattei, Francesca Fallucchi, Fabio Massimo Zanzotto
arxiv-2201-05613.description: Abstract Pre-trained Transformers are challenging human performances in many NLP tasks. The massive datasets used for pre-training seem to be the key to their success on existing tasks. In this paper, we explore how a range of pre-trained Natural Language Understanding models perform on definitely unseen sentences provided by classification tasks over a DarkNet corpus.

arxiv-2202-13693.title: Explainable deepfake and spoofing detection: an attack analysis using SHapley Additive exPlanations
arxiv-2202-13693.description: Abstract Despite several years of research in deepfake and spoofing detection for automatic speaker verification, little is known about the artefacts that classifiers use to distinguish between bona fide and spoofed utterances. An understanding of these is crucial to the design of trustworthy, explainable solutions.

arxiv-2204-07342.title: Curvature-driven instabilities in thin active shells
arxiv-2204-07342.creator: Andrea Giudici 1 , John S. Biggins 1
arxiv-2204-07342.description: Abstract Spontaneous material shape changes, such as swelling, growth or thermal expansion, can be used to trigger dramatic elastic instabilities in thin shells. These instabilities originate in geometric incompatibility between the preferred extrinsic and intrinsic curvature of the shell, which may be modified by active deformations through the thickness and in plane respectively.

arxiv-2207-02597.title: Cooperative Beam Selection for RIS-Aided Terahertz MIMO Networks via Multi-Task Learning
arxiv-2207-02597.creator: Xinying Ma, Gong Chen, Xiaofei Wang
arxiv-2207-02597.description: Abstract Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) have been cast as a promising alternative to alleviate blockage vulnerability and enhance coverage capability for terahertz (THz) communications. Owing to large-scale array elements at transceivers and RIS, the codebook based beamforming can be utilized in a computationally efficient manner. However, the codeword selection for analog beamforming is an intractable combinatorial optimization (CO) problem.

arxiv-2403-02483.title: Opinion inertia and coarsening in the Persistent Voter model
arxiv-2403-02483.creator: Luís Carlos F. Latoski, W. G. Dantas, Jeferson J. Arenzon
arxiv-2403-02483.description: Abstract We consider the Persistent Voter model (PVM), a variant of the Voter model (VM) that includes transient, dynamically-induced zealots. Due to peer reinforcement, the internal confidence η i \eta_{i} of a normal voter increases by steps of size Δ ​ η \Delta\eta and once it gets above a given threshold, it becomes a zealot.

arxiv-2411-13596.title: End-to-End Multi-Track Reconstruction using Graph Neural Networks at Belle II
arxiv-2411-13596.creator: L. Reuter, G. De Pietro, S. Stefkova, T. Ferber, V. Bertacchi, G. Casarosa, L. Corona, P. Ecker, A. Glazov, Y. Han, M. Laurenza, T. Lueck, L. Massaccesi, S. Mondal, B. Scavino, S. Spataro, C. Wessel, L. Zani
arxiv-2411-13596.description: Abstract We present the study of an end-to-end multi-track reconstruction algorithm for the central drift chamber of the Belle II experiment at the SuperKEKB collider using Graph Neural Networks for an unknown number of particles. The algorithm uses detector hits as inputs without pre-filtering to simultaneously predict the number of track candidates in an event and their kinematic properties.

arxiv-2501-13864.title: Autoencoders for Anomaly Detection are Unreliable
arxiv-2501-13864.creator: Roel Bouman & Tom Heskes
arxiv-2501-13864.description: Abstract Autoencoders are frequently used for anomaly detection, both in the unsupervised and semi-supervised settings. They rely on the assumption that when trained using the reconstruction loss, they will be able to reconstruct normal data more accurately than anomalous data.

arxiv-2508-21437.title: Trees as Gaussians: Large-Scale Individual Tree Mapping
arxiv-2508-21437.creator: Dimitri Gominski, Martin Brandt, Xiaoye Tong, Siyu Liu, Maurice Mugabowindekwe, Sizhuo Li, Florian Reiner, Andrew Davies, Rasmus Fensholt
arxiv-2508-21437.description: Abstract Trees are key components of the terrestrial biosphere, playing vital roles in ecosystem function, climate regulation, and the bioeconomy. However, large-scale monitoring of individual trees remains limited by inadequate modelling. Available global products have focused on binary tree cover or canopy height, which do not explicitely identify trees at individual level.

arxiv-2510-01502.title: Aligning Video Models with Human Social Judgments via Behavior-Guided Fine-Tuning
arxiv-2510-01502.creator: Kathy Garcia, & Leyla Isik
arxiv-2510-01502.description: Abstract Humans intuitively perceive complex social signals in visual scenes, yet it remains unclear whether state-of-the-art AI models encode the same similarity structure. We study (Q1) whether modern video and language models capture human-perceived similarity in social videos, and (Q2) how to instill this structure into models using human behavioral data.

Human serum is a rich source of readily accessible EVs;...

plos-pone-0000204.description: PLOS ONE research article. Ancient Origin of the New Developmental Superfamily DANGER

pmc-10600394.title: Aging, longevity, and the role of environmental stressors: a focus on wildfire smoke and air quality
pmc-10600394.creator: David Scieszka, Alicia M. Bolt, Mark A. McCormick, Jonathan L. Brigman, Matthew J. Campen
pmc-10600394.description: Aging is a complex biological process involving multiple interacting mechanisms and is being increasingly linked to environmental exposures such as wildfire smoke. In this review, we detail the hallmarks of aging, emphasizing the role of telomere attrition, cellular senescence, epigenetic alterations, proteostasis, genomic instability, and mitochondrial dysfunction, while also exploring integrative hallmarks - altered intercellular communication and stem cell exhaustion.

pmc-10609960.title: Heparin Precursors with Reduced Anticoagulant Properties Retain Antiviral and Protective Effects That Potentiate the Efficacy of Sofosbuvir against Zika Virus Infection in Human Neural Progenitor Cells
pmc-10609960.creator: Isabel Pagani, Linda Ottoboni, Paola Panina-Bordignon, Gianvito Martino, Guido Poli, Sarah Taylor, Jeremy E Turnbull, Edwin Yates, Elisa Vicenzi, Deirdre R Coombe
pmc-10609960.description: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection during pregnancy can result in severe birth defects, such as microcephaly, as well as a range of other related health complications. Heparin, a clinical-grade anticoagulant, is shown to protect neural progenitor cells from death following ZIKV infection. Although heparin can be safely used during pregnancy, it retains off-target anticoagulant effects if directly employed against ZIKV infection.

pmc-11393565.title: Acute necrotizing pancreatitis caused by ampullary cancer: a case report
pmc-11393565.creator: Miguel A Moyon, Tatiana B Fernandez, Carlos Julio Lopez, Luis F Flores, Jose A Rosales, William Aguayo, Christian Rojas, Gabriel A Molina
pmc-11393565.description: Ampullary malignancies are extremely rare tumors that are usually diagnosed when they cause biliary obstruction. Rarely, any tumor or mass near or within the pancreas can cause acute pancreatitis and on even rarer occasions, these tumors can cause severe complications such as acute peripancreatic fluid collections, necrotizing pancreatitis, and infections.

pmc-11480348.title: A semi-transparent thermoelectric glazing nanogenerator with aluminium doped zinc oxide and copper iodide thin films
pmc-11480348.creator: Mustafa Majid Rashak Al-Fartoos, Anurag Roy, Tapas K. Mallick, Asif Ali Tahir
pmc-11480348.description: To address the pressing need for reducing building energy consumption and combating climate change, thermoelectric glazing (TEGZ) presents a promising solution. This technology harnesses waste heat from buildings and converts it into electricity, while maintaining comfortable indoor temperatures. Here, we developed a TEGZ using cost-effective materials, specifically aluminium-doped zinc oxide (AZO) and copper iodide (CuI).

pmc-11487154.title: Melatonin as a potential adjunct therapy for central nervous system lupus: evidence from the MRL/lpr mouse model
pmc-11487154.creator: Jaivarshaan Rajkumar, Alexandra Spath, Hyndevi Dokuri, Alexander Jacob, Richard John Quigg, Jessy John Alexander
pmc-11487154.description: Despite advancements in treatment strategies, individuals with SLE still face a significantly reduced life expectancy. Current treatments, such as immunosuppressants and corticosteroids, are effective but carry risks of severe side effects, including malignancies. This highlights the urgent need for innovative therapeutic approaches.

pmc-12406389.title: Explanatory spatial modeling of COVID-19 vaccine coverage in Thailand: policy implications for equitable distribution
pmc-12406389.creator: Kittipong Sornlorm, Sarayu Muntaphan
pmc-12406389.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic posed significant challenges globally, with vaccine distribution being a critical factor for recovery. Despite achieving vaccination targets, Thailand faced disparities in vaccine coverage across regions. This study aims to explore spatial clustering patterns and examine socioeconomic, demographic, and health service-related determinants of COVID-19 vaccine coverage across Thailand.

pmc-12415068.title: Changes in potential pathogenicity-associated proteins of Helicobacter cinaedi upon infection of macrophage cells
pmc-12415068.creator: A. K. Voronina, B. A. Efimov, M. V. Malakhova, P. V. Shnaider, O. M. Ivanova, M. Bogomiakova, V. O. Shender, M. A. Lagarkova, G. P. Arapidi
pmc-12415068.description: IntroductionHelicobacter cinaedi is a spiral-shaped Gram-negative, enterohepatic bacterium classified as a conditional pathogen (pathogenicity group 2). It is known to cause bacteremia and a variety of other diseases in humans. In particular, Helicobacter cinaedi has been shown to impair intracellular cholesterol metabolism when interacting with macrophages, leading to foam cell formation.

pmc-12711890.title: Intestinal bacteria trigger a hibernation-like state in homotherms via the gut-brain axis
pmc-12711890.creator: Ziqiang Bao, Cheng Guo, Yi Chen, Tao Lei, Hua Peng, Han Zhang, Xiaofei Zhang, Ying Ban, Dunwu Qi, Juntao Feng, Zuofu Xiang
pmc-12711890.description: The adaptation to low temperature has research value in the fields of spaceflight, disease treatment, and ecological evolution. However, continuous exposure to cold leads to hypothermia and death in homothermic animals. Interestingly, heterothermic animals can easily overcome this challenge. We transferred intestinal bacteria from hibernating Marmota himalayana into mice (homothermic animals) and successfully induced a torpor-like state.

pmc-13221529.title: Competitive roles of plasticity, elasticity, and radiation in heat/mass transfer of Casson–Williamson–Maxwell nanofluid over a porous stretching sheet
pmc-13221529.creator: R Kavitha, Ravi Samikannu, Nyagong Santino David Ladu
pmc-13221529.description: In this paper, Casson–Williamson and Maxwell fluid flow over a stretching porous sheet is investigated numerically, taking into account the effects of thermal radiation, thermophoresis, magnetohydrodynamics (MHD), and chemical processes. The flow, heat transfer, and mass diffusion controlling partial differential equations (PDEs) are converted into ordinary differential equations (ODEs) by use of a similarity transformation.

pmc-13228140.title: Using large language models to enhance clinically-driven missing data recovery algorithms in electronic health records
pmc-13228140.creator: Sarah C Lotspeich, Abbey N Collins, Brian J Wells, Ashish K Khanna, Joseph Rigdon, Lucy D’Agostino McGowan
pmc-13228140.description: ObjectivesElectronic health record (EHR) data are prone to missingness and errors. Previously, we devised an enriched chart review protocol where a “roadmap” of auxiliary diagnoses was used to recover missing values. Still, chart reviews are expensive and time-intensive, limiting the number of patients whose data can be reviewed.

pmc-13263017.title: Association Between Electronic Health Record–Based Nursing Workload and Turnover: Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13263017.creator: Linlin Xia, Daphne Lew, Lindsay Tessmer, Elise Eiden, Sunny Lou, Thomas Kannampallil, Elizabeth Borycki
pmc-13263017.description: BackgroundNurse turnover remains a major challenge for health systems, yet objective, scalable measures of workload that predict turnover are limited. Electronic health record (EHR) audit logs offer a potential data source to quantify nursing work patterns.ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the association between EHR-derived measures of nursing workload and turnover among inpatient nurses.
